# Tidepool Landing Page: Build Plan

**Overall direction:** Calm, tidal, and organized. The page should feel like a shared whiteboard at the start of a good week, not a corporate SaaS grid.

**Palette:** Deep tide teal (#0F3D3E) for text and footers, sand (#F5EFE6) as the main background, foam (#E3F1EC) for alternating bands, coral (#E8795B) for CTAs only.

**Type:** Fraunces (variable serif) for headlines at 56–72px on desktop. Inter for body at 18px with 1.6 line height. Keep line lengths under 65 characters.

**Imagery:** Soft, hand-drawn tide-line dividers between sections. No stock photos of people at laptops. Use a real product screenshot of the week board, cropped at an angle with a subtle shadow.

---

**1. Navigation**
Single row: wordmark left, three links (Product, Pricing, Teams), "Log in" text link, and a coral "Start free" button right. Transparent over sand, solidifies on scroll.

**2. Hero**
Two columns, text left, screenshot right. Headline: "Your team's week, finally in one tide." Subhead: "Tidepool helps small teams plan the week together in fifteen minutes on Monday morning." Primary CTA "Start your first week," secondary "See how it works." Under the CTA, a single line: "Free for teams up to five."

**3. Problem strip**
Full-width foam band, centered, one sentence in serif: "Most weekly plans live in six tabs and a group chat that nobody scrolls." Copy should name the pain without blame.

**4. How it works**
Three horizontal cards with numbered tide-stone icons. Steps: "Gather your week" (add what's on everyone's plate), "Shape the plan" (drag items into shared days), "Check the tide" (a Friday glance at what moved). Each card: one verb-led heading, two sentences max.

**5. Feature showcase**
Alternating layout. Large screenshot of the week board with annotations in coral callouts. Copy: "See everyone's week at once. No meeting required." Follow with two smaller feature rows: async standup notes and carry-over tracking.

**6. Team proof**
Sand background. Three short quotes from small-team leads, each with first name, role, and team size. Set in Fraunces italic. Add a counter: "2,400 weeks planned."

**7. Pricing teaser**
Two cards side by side: Free (up to five people) and Team ($8/seat/month). No comparison table on the homepage. Link to full pricing.

**8. FAQ**
Accordion, five questions: integrations, privacy, mobile, switching from other tools, and cancellation. Answers in plain language.

**9. Final CTA**
Deep teal full-bleed band with sand text. Headline: "Plan Monday before Monday starts." Single coral button. Tide-line illustration bleeding off the bottom edge.

**10. Footer**
Four columns (Product, Company, Resources, Legal) on teal. Small wordmark and a one-line sign-off: "Built for teams who'd rather be doing the work."

# Tidepool Landing Page: Revised Build Plan

**Goal:** Convert small-team leads (3–15 people) who already feel weekly planning chaos into a free trial. Every section should answer one question: "Can my team actually do this on Monday?"

**Palette:** Deep tide teal (#0F3D3E) for headlines and footer. Sand (#F5EFE6) as the base background. Foam (#E3F1EC) for alternating bands. Coral (#D9664A) for CTAs only, with teal text on it to pass WCAG AA contrast (white on the original coral fails).

**Type:** Fraunces for headlines (56–72px desktop, 36–40px mobile). Inter for body at 18px, 1.6 line height, 65-character max line length. Fraunces italic is reserved for quotes.

**Imagery:** Hand-drawn tide-line dividers between sections. No stock photos of people at laptops. Use a real, angled screenshot of the week board with a soft shadow. Show realistic names and tasks, not lorem ipsum.

---

**1. Navigation**
Wordmark left, three links (Product, Pricing, Teams), "Log in" text link, and a coral "Start free" button right. Transparent over sand, solidifies on scroll. Collapses to a menu icon below 768px.

**2. Hero**
Two columns: text left, screenshot right (stacks on mobile with the screenshot below). Headline: "Plan your team's week before Monday gets away from you." Subhead: "Tidepool gives small teams one shared week, built together in about fifteen minutes." Primary CTA: "Start your first week." Secondary text link: "Watch a 90-second tour." Beneath: "Free for teams up to five. No card required."

**3. Problem strip**
Full-width foam band, centered serif sentence: "Most weekly plans live in six tabs and a group chat nobody scrolls." No blame, no adjectives about the team.

**4. How it works**
Three cards with numbered tide-stone icons. "Gather what's on everyone's plate." "Shape the week into shared days." "Check the tide on Friday." Each heading is a verb phrase, body is two sentences maximum. Cards sit on a sand background with a thin teal top border.

**5. Feature showcase**
Alternating rows. First: large screenshot with coral-numbered callouts pointing to real UI elements. Copy: "Everyone's week, visible at once. No meeting required." Second and third rows, smaller: async standup notes and carry-over tracking, each with a 15-second looping GIF.

**6. Proof**
Sand background. Three quotes in Fraunces italic, each with first name, role, and team size. Use only real, permissioned quotes. Omit the "weeks planned" counter until the number is verified; an unsupported stat undermines the page.

**7. Pricing teaser**
Two cards: Free (up to five people) and Team ($8 per seat per month). Each lists three bullets. No comparison table here. Link to full pricing below.

**8. FAQ**
Accordion with five questions: integrations, privacy, mobile, switching from other tools, cancellation. Answers under 40 words, plain language. Keep the privacy answer specific about data retention.

**9. Final CTA**
Deep teal full-bleed band, sand text. Headline: "Plan Monday before Monday starts." One coral button. Tide-line illustration bleeds off the bottom edge.

**10. Footer**
Four columns (Product, Company, Resources, Legal) on teal. Wordmark and the sign-off "Built for teams who'd rather be doing the work."
